interpretation: For deterministic greedy proposal d, q(d)=1: accept with target probability p(d); rejection samples target p renormalized excluding d. The resulting ideal arithmetic marginal is p. Draft FP8 can change d/acceptance/speed without changing ideal target marginal. T0 instead verifies target argmax. Both statements assume the correct target probabilities and correct implementation.
limitations: Analytic/source audit, not empirical GPU distribution, RNG independence or agent-success proof.
Actual sampled target math still includes selected short-row dense FP8 and quantized expert weights; BF16 cache/output does not make it a BF16 model.
A fixed seed does not guarantee identical outputs across proposal schedules; this run also observed variation in flag-off repeat controls. Strict seed identity remained failed, not waived.
Full verification-width changes can alter target floating math/shape dispatch, so deterministic-proposal theorem does not prove cross-width target parity. Narrow is excluded.
